title: US and Mexico lose measles-free status
summary: The United States lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization has said. Bolivia and Mexico have also lost their measles elimination status.

image.caption: Measles, a highly contagious virus, has spread in the US largely among the unvaccinated at the highest rate in more than 30 yearsImage: Sean Rayford/Getty Images/AFP

blocks.text: The ​United States is experiencing its highest number ​of cases in more than three decades. Some 7,700 people in the country have been infected and 13 have died since 2025.

As ​of November 12, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have confirmed 5,412 measles cases and 6 deaths. US states have reported a total of 10 deaths from the highly contagious virus, this year.
Thanks to a series of functioning vaccines, measles had been virtually eradicated throughout most of the developed world for decades.
